text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock fell 3.9% today, continuing a sharp two-week decline of over 11%. The immediate driver appears to be oil prices dropping on news of renewed U.S.-Iran peace efforts easing Middle East supply concerns — crude fell from around $110+ in recent days toward $103 per barrel. For a refiner, lower oil prices sound good in theory, but refiners profit most when the gap between crude costs and refined product prices (gasoline, diesel) widens; when crude drops fast, refined product prices often don't keep pace, squeezing margins.

Adding to the pressure, CNBC reported that Big Oil earnings guidance is drawing investor caution ahead of results, suggesting the market may be bracing for weaker-than-expected outlooks from the sector. With refineries running at 92.8% capacity and product inventories relatively high (gasoline and diesel storage both above seasonal norms), there's less room for pricing power even as crude retreats.
